batch: September 14, 2026 — New folder DMR, NPDES application and SIU intake
methods: Verified SHA-256, byte size, PDF metadata and page counts for all eight supplied PDFs.
Rendered every page in source order at 120 DPI and visually inspected all 85 rendered pages; no unreadable pages were found.

Checked embedded text page-by-page. All 85 pages contained usable native text, so OCR was not required; visual inspection confirmed the SIU tables, NPDES application tables, DMR measurement grids, certification blocks and blank fields.

Compared normalized page text, page counts and rendered content against the existing canonical IPP, NPDES and DMR assets. The SIU list and NPDES application are content-equivalent byte-distinct variants; the six GW1010342 DMRs are byte-identical to their canonical assets.

Applied substantive classifications and cross-source tie-backs while preserving each supplied filename, source hash, rendered-page coverage and the distinction between reported measurements, permit/application representations and later cessation comments.

records.contentClassification: SIU/CIU roster, contacts and regulatory flags
records.finding: The six-page 2019 roster identifies 21 industrial-user sites. Wexford County Landfill LLC is listed at 990 N US Hwy 131, Manton, Wexford County, Michigan 49663, with American Waste as the legal name, Terry Whetstone as Landfill Manager, and the landfill classified as an SIU with local limits applicable. The roster also records Cadillac-area facility addresses, SIC/NAICS fields, contacts and emails. Its category codes include CIU entries for the four AAR locations, Cadillac Castings, Cadillac Renewable Energy, Munson Healthcare and Rec Boat Trailer; the source preserves the roster’s spelling and address anomalies.
records.boundary: A roster snapshot is administrative identity and program-scope evidence, not proof of a load, discharge, PFAS use, violation or source attribution. The Avon Protection ZIP shown as 46901 and spellings such as “Arvco Container Corperation” and “Munson Heath Care” are preserved rather than corrected.

leadTrace.lead: Wexford’s SIU identity and contact link the landfill to the 2017 NPDES application and the 2018 PFAS screening workflow.
leadTrace.targetRecords: 2017-04-03 Cadillac WWTP NPDES application; 2018 IPP screening/update; American Waste PFAS survey; Wexford leachate and groundwater-discharge records
leadTrace.tieBack: Use the roster only to reconcile entity, address and contact identity; use the dated application, survey, monitoring, DMR and analytical records for volumes, sampling and results.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The roster contains no transaction-level hauling data, sample result or causal determination.

records.contentClassification: Cadillac WWTP NPDES permit-reissuance application and attachments index
records.finding: The April 3, 2017 submission (2Q7-HQ21-P66B, permit MI0020257) identifies the Cadillac WWTP at 1121 Plett Road, a certified operator (Jeffrey Dietlin, certification 10435), an outfall to the Clam River (HUC 04060102), and continuous design flow of 3.2 MGD. It reports three prior annual-average flows of 2.034, 1.937 and 1.943 MGD with maximum daily flows of 3.719, 2.654 and 3.263 MGD. Section 10 reports 1.5 MGD total nondomestic wastewater, with 0.486 MGD each for industrial process, contact-cooling and noncontact-cooling water and 0.04 MGD landfill leachate. The form says an IPP is required, lists a 2000 sewer-use ordinance, 1993 interjurisdictional agreements, 1993 local limits, 179.73 dry tons generated/treated/applied in the biosolids section, and includes reported biosolids metals, nutrients and pathogen data. It identifies the Clam River as the storm-water receiving water, says no industrial materials are exposed, and names Jeff Dietlin as the storm-water certified operator.
records.boundary: The application records applicant representations and a list of referenced attachments; it is not itself a delivery log, laboratory report, proof of permit issuance, or proof that a particular leachate load occurred. The listed SIU, process-flow, lab and biosolids attachments were not included in this upload and remain separate records to verify individually. Storage capacity is entered as 1,214,091 without a visible unit selection in the extracted field, so no unit is inferred.

leadTrace.lead: The 0.04 MGD landfill-leachate entry provides an application-era average-volume baseline.
leadTrace.targetRecords: GW1010342 DMR daily and summary records; Wexford receiving/hauling and leachate-finance records
leadTrace.tieBack: Compare this average-volume representation with the groundwater-permit cap and the dated GW1010342 DMR flow entries; do not convert it into individual deliveries or a total without a separate log.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The application does not identify the measurement period or individual loads behind the 0.04 MGD entry.

leadTrace.lead: Section 11 lists 21 SIU attachment files and Section 12 lists two Kar Lab biosolids reports.
leadTrace.targetRecords: IPP SIU profiles; biosolids laboratory records; process-flow and WET-test attachments
leadTrace.tieBack: Treat the attachment list as a retrieval lead and verify each supplied attachment separately; the application does not reproduce their contents.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The current upload contains only the application, not the listed attachment payloads.

queueDecision: All eight uploads are already represented by canonical public records. Six GW1010342 DMR PDFs are byte-identical; the 2019 SIU/CIU list and 2017 NPDES application are content-equivalent byte-distinct variants. The reread adds no new source asset or independent event, so no duplicate cards or timeline events were created. The supplied filenames, hashes, page coverage and substantive findings are retained here for provenance and verification.
evidentiaryBoundary: This batch strengthens the documented chain from SIU identity and NPDES representations to permittee-submitted groundwater-discharge monitoring. It does not independently prove a leachate load, PFAS concentration, permit violation, causal source attribution, or legal termination beyond what each source reports.
